junk_imagery.evidence: hook@0.3 through seg1:end: the 'Room temperature 293' grid tiles are identical purple starfield-and-mountain clip-art squares. They have nothing to do with room temperature, which makes them generic filler icons.

decorative_mascot.evidence: seg1:start to seg1:end: Data stands in the middle of the tile grid holding a red stamp but never stamps or places a tile. seg2: he stands on top of the circle with his hands on his head. seg3: he stands on top of the square. None of these is a setup, action and payoff tied to the stat.

bare_number_card.evidence: seg2:start to seg2:end: a plain teal circle labelled only '1' grows next to '0.0 NASA Cold Atom Lab'. seg3:start to seg3:end: a full-frame teal square reads '29400T' with nothing else in it.

dead_air.evidence: seg0:mid to seg1:end (t=2.2 to 8.2s): the grid is complete and frozen. Only Data's arm twitches, so about 6s of the same frame. seg3:start to seg3:end (t=16.6 to 20.3s): the square is unchanged. The measured held_s is 4.0.

empty_void.evidence: seg2:start: a small circle and a tiny '0.0' label float in a large dark field. seg4:start: the ruler and ladder sit in a mostly empty dark frame.

unreadable.evidence: seg4:mid to payoff@-0.4: '29,399,999,999,999,752 apa' is cut off by the right frame edge. 'NASA's Cold ...' is truncated. seg2:mid: 'NASA Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' is tiny and sits against the circle's edge. seg3:start: 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' is printed on top of the teal square.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: A full-frame flat teal square with the meaningless label '29400T' in the centre. Data stands idle on top, and a tiny overlapping label reads 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)'. Nothing changes for about 4s while the narration talks about 5,000 light-years versus 250 miles up.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The distance comparison (5,000 light-years versus 250 miles) went to a generic area-square machine. That machine shows only one value, with a unit-mangled abbreviation, and has no second object to compare against.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Draw the distance as a SHOT. Earth with the ISS at 250 miles, then a zoom-out where Data hauls a measuring tape from the ISS out toward a far nebula that dwarfs the frame. The headline should be one readable number ('5,000 light-years' versus '250 miles'), and no label should overlap a mark.

depictions.note: A unit grid of generic starfield tiles ('each = 20') for room temperature. The icon has no link to the subject, and the 2.7K space value never appears.
The same frozen tile grid repeats. Nothing shows deep space at 2.7.
A circle sized '1' against '0.0'. A proportional-area bubble asserts nothing about 'a billion times colder'.
A flat area square reading '29400T'. The unit is garbled and there is no comparison object.
A ruler on a ladder that Data stretches is a stock measure machine. The giant cut-off number undoes it.

grades.one_line: Generic charts and a frozen clip-art grid with garbled labels ('29400T', '0.0', a cut-off number) never show how cold or how far anything is.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3) opens on a static tile grid labelled 'Room temperature 293'. The visuals give no reason to stay.
seg0 and seg1 repeat the same frozen grid for about 7s, and the 2.7K deep-space value is never drawn.
seg2's 'Coldest atom lab' bubble reads '1' versus '0.0', which is meaningless and contradicts the narration.
seg3 shows '29400T' on a full-frame flat square. The unit is garbled and the label overlaps the square.
seg4's '29,399,999,999,999,752 apa' is clipped at the frame edge, and 'NASA's Cold ...' is truncated.
Data stands idle on top of shapes in seg2 and seg3, and his stamp in seg0 and seg1 never stamps anything.
fixes: Hook: open with the ISS orbiting Earth and a frost burst. Data in a parka points the camera up at a thermometer plunging.
seg0 and seg1: show a thermometer Data pumps down from 293 to 2.7, so the drop is a visible distance.
seg2: show a billion-fold scale. Data cranks a freezer dial while the scale zooms past space's 2.7K to 100 pK. Drop '1 vs 0.0'.
seg3: replace the square with an Earth–ISS–nebula distance shot. Data pulls a tape measure. Use one readable headline.
seg4: format the payoff number in human units that fit inside the frame, and fix the truncated labels.
